entries.topic: Explanation and mixed PDA/Office network HA safety audit for Agent PRIMARY/NEXT_A/NEXT_B
facts: HA leadership in active main and PR606 is Firestore relay_poc_coordination/roles with generation and update-time CAS, not network-name/Wi-Fi preference. PRIMARY writes RTDB heartbeat approximately 10s; if failed writes existing Firestore lease. NEXT_A consumes RTDB SSE and when freshness unknown checks Firestore lease; 15s is a suspicion threshold, not guaranteed takeover completion.

Automatic NEXT_A takeover requires relay schedule enabled, local WMS ready, a fresh WMS browser readiness probe and a successful Firestore generation-fenced CAS. NEXT_B is second standby and is not documented as an immediate independent self-promoter without role promotion.

When PRIMARY WMS is unready, it retains PRIMARY for at least two samples separated by >=15s; with a ready standby it may write handoff roles and relinquish. Without a standby it can remain DEGRADED_RECEIVER and ACK WMS_SESSION_REQUIRED without WMS mutation. Startup with vacant roles may elect WMS-unready degraded PRIMARY; business mutation always demands local WMS-ready and fresh Firebase PRIMARY generation.

Critical mixed-network limitation: an Office NEXT_A with Firestore reachable but RTDB probe blocked (403/network) returns UNAVAILABLE on ProbePrimary, and VerifyPrimaryDownBeforeTakeover explicitly defers even after stale Firestore lease. This prevents unsafe split-brain but means automatic failover can remain unavailable when PRIMARY disappears. Network class itself neither guarantees nor forbids PRIMARY: both Firebase control reachability and WMS authenticated readiness are required.

RTDB heartbeat payload currently writes wms_ready=true unconditionally even during potential degraded PRIMARY readiness; local role WMS readiness is checked separately. This is a diagnostic representation mismatch, not evidence that this flag is used to approve WMS mutations. Review only with Owner-approved cross-component change.

D168WorkerSession Wi-Fi handoff is task-scoped, user/approved-profile gated, restores original Wi-Fi and is distinct from HA leadership or a fleet-wide automatic PRIMARY migration. Existing Firebase Office critical path must remain.
No field simulation of a cross-network failover and no new release is asserted. No code, provider routing, Stable, Beta/Agent/APK release or PR merge is approved by this informational answer.

entries.topic: Reduce Firestore HA lease usage in cross-network PDA/Office RTDB-unreachable deployment
facts: Current source writes PRIMARY heartbeat to RTDB at ~10s and writes Firestore lease only on RTDB write failure or ancillary actions; NEXT_A uses SSE when fresh and falls back to Firestore lease GET when RTDB stale. RTDB observer retries at 1s after failures. Firestore CheckPrimaryLease schedules as low as ~1s and, with absent/stale Firestore lease, attempts RTDB probe each 5s; if Office RTDB probe is UNAVAILABLE takeover is deferred for safety even though PRIMARY might have died.

The D169-E010 Oct 15 archived v132 NEXT_A 4h48 sample counted 3258 PRIMARY_LEASE_READ attempts, 3255 stale-RTDB fallback, 531 SSE timeouts and 52 HTTP_403, not provider authoritative billing; treat as strong repeated-read hotspot, not billable cost total.

Proposed first optimization: RTDB capability classification by actual connection outcome, response class and authentication, bounded jittered exponential backoff or circuit-breaker on persistently unreachable Office RTDB, immediate re-probe on connectivity or session/network changes. This reduces futile SSE connects and local/log churn, but ALONE does not lower required Firestore lease GET and must not suppress liveness safety.

Proposed main solution: conditional mixed-network dual liveness when any eligible NEXT_A cannot access RTDB: PRIMARY publishes a bounded Firestore heartbeat even if own RTDB is healthy, then use adaptive deadline-based Firestore lease observation by NEXT_A, possible existing authenticated Firestore listener only when proven reachable and billable operations compared. Continue generation-fenced roles CAS and WMS readiness/mutation fences. Firestore is still authoritative cross-network and does not require an unregistered service or Office Cloudflare connectivity. No fixed new cadence authorized without failure-bound latency analysis.

Eliminate dangerous RTDB dependency in mixed-network takeover only after proving Firestore-dual-heartbeat and authoritative role/generation fencing, transaction idempotency and partition invariants for PRIMARY Firestore-loss, stale Office lease, simultaneous standby candidates, restart, old Agent coexistence. Firestore lease expiry cannot authorize takeover by itself when published path/actual PRIMARY state is uncertain.

Alternative network-aware primary/standby affinity can prefer PDA RTDB-capable peers and keep Office NEXT_B for lower overhead but fails to guarantee cross-network takeover; do not rely on as sole HA. Firestore document listener requires an Office-network gRPC/transport proof and is not no-cost: every updated observed document can count a read under Standard edition.

Firestore Standard free-tier reference from Firebase documentation currently 50k reads/day and 20k writes/day, but fleet/provider actual billing and database plan not established. Do not claim a specific percentage of provider savings from local counters or shift reads into writes without estimating full daily fleet traffic.

No source, network routes, consumer behavior, new timer/service or Beta/Stable runtime edited; preserve Office Firebase critical path and release OWNER-GATED. Owner explicit approval required for actual HA changes.

entries.topic: Owner proposal to classify Agent network profiles by exact SSID, avoid RTDB capability probing on known Office SSIDs
facts: Owner states company Wi-Fi names are stable, proposes a locally configurable allowlist of internal Office SSIDs and automatic network-class policy selection based on actual Windows-connected SSID, without repeated synthetic connectivity probes; Agent must distinguish known internal Office from PDA/Internet and unknown safely.

Existing main/PR606 Program.cs GetSsid runs netsh wlan show interfaces but SSID currently used primarily for UI/status; D168NetworkRoute.cs stores up to 6 locally approved Wi-Fi profiles for controlled Worker task handoff, not general SSID-to-HA transport routing. Existing 2026-10-13 Owner decision used actual endpoint capability rather than SSID as a generic network policy; new Owner clarification proposes SSID as a routing policy hint, not security authority.

Proposed exact SSID mapping with local Windows WLAN-change signals/on-login, no fast netsh polling, no per-cycle RTDB probe for configured Office profiles. Known PDA/Internet uses RTDB HA; known Office uses Firestore HA; unknown/multiple adapters/Ethernet/VPN unresolved fail closed and allow explicit classification. No SSID/password/profile values or user identifiers in public repo, raw logs, or telemetry.

Cross-network HA must consider BOTH local NEXT_A classification AND PRIMARY network mode: if PRIMARY on PDA RTDB but NEXT_A on Office Firestore-only, PRIMARY must conditionally publish Firestore liveness (or another preexisting trusted shared signal) or Office cannot safely verify and promote. If PRIMARY on Office Firestore, Internet NEXT_A must consume Firestore evidence, not assume RTDB. Role/generation CAS, WMS browser readiness and before-mutation Firestore fencing remain mandatory and not inferred from SSID.

Static SSID labels replace capability-probe loops only for normal transport routing; they do not prove network service availability, WMS authorization, a live PRIMARY or permission to execute business. Actual business errors handled through existing calls without synthetic ping; policy must degrade safely if misclassified, Wi-Fi association changes, proxy/VPN, wired network or SSID spoofing.

Cost reality: disabled RTDB retries save futile network attempts/CPU/log but do not by themselves reduce Firestore reads. Cross-network 15s HA requires bounded shared liveness updates; adaptively bounded reads, listener transport feasibility and provider-billing comparison needed before estimating savings. No unregistered new channel or unauthorized direct main/Stable release.

entries.topic: Free-quota alternatives to Firestore HA liveness for Office blocked RTDB
facts: Confirmed Oct 15 NEXT_A local HA fallback sample: 3258 lease GET attempts over ~4h48; one-second SSE reconnects and Firestore fallback are waste hotspots but not authoritative billable usage.

Office reachability currently evidenced for Firestore, not RTDB/Cloudflare/PubSub/Ably/Supabase; all alternative services are hypothetical until authorized Office-network read-only access test. SSID-based known Office mode avoids futile RTDB probing but cannot by itself replace authenticated liveness or Firestore roles/generation fencing.

Official Firebase Firestore Standard no-cost daily quota: 50000 document reads and 20000 writes; official RTDB no-cost 1GB stored and 10GB/month downloaded, not per operation. A single cross-network 10s Firestore heartbeat incurs ~8640 writes/day and each NEXT_A 10s observation ~8640 reads/day if 24h; 15s suspicion latency cannot be promised by slower polling.

Official Google Cloud Pub/Sub Basic offers first 10GiB monthly delivery/ingest throughput at no cost (with per-request minimum and any storage/transfer ancillary pricing), but Office access, gRPC/HTTP2, IAM and duplicate/out-of-order semantics require verification; message delivery cannot substitute for Firestore generation-fenced authority.

Official Ably Free 6M messages/month and 200 concurrent connections; Supabase Free 2M realtime messages/month and 200 concurrent connections but can pause low-activity projects; Cloudflare Durable Objects Free 100k requests/day and SQLite rows usage, existing Worker route not confirmed Office-reachable. None shown to operate from Office; neither service may be deployed without registered resource scope/Owner approval.

Lowest-change optimization: prefer RTDB-capable PDA pair PRIMARY/NEXT_A where available; known Office networks skip RTDB reconnect loop; explore one existing Firestore listener/mode or piggyback existing authorized periodic writes, but Firestore listener is billed a read for each updated document; cross-network needs live common evidence, no magical cost removal. Stronger alternative Google Pub/Sub only if Office supports it; keep Firestore CAS as business safety authority.
No changes to Agent, Firebase, Worker, public endpoints, Stable, PR606 merge or release are authorized or undertaken.

Visible read rows leave 5514 unattributed. Firebase quota-period view ~24k reads/4.2k writes/564 deletes and RTDB/billing-period views have different scopes; never add them. Billing Overview shows approximately VND679 gross, VND678 savings and VND1 net for Oct1–16, not final invoice or 24h Firestore cost.

SOURCE_CONFIRMED stronger finding than E010/E006: only discovered LoadOpen caller is ReconcileD134AgentSync; LoadLegacyAlerts reads status PENDING/SENT LIMIT100, skips chat/expiry after read and returns IsActiveCall=false; sole Reconcile consumer skips !IsActiveCall. Thus this legacy-read branch currently contributes no active-call output. Two distinct PRIMARY samples show 32 queries+3168 extra docs=3200 estimated reads and 53+5247=5300; this supports removing the unused reconcile read while retaining real active-call/chat/FCM paths, subject to approval/regression. It does not authorize deletion of alerts or FCM retirement.

Morning Oct16 NEXT_A local audit: 1745 lease-read attempts, 8589 RTDB SSE HTTP403, 1743 takeover-probe UNAVAILABLE; concurrent Firestore sync/presence events prove existing listener activity. Prior Oct15 NEXT_A sample had 3258 lease attempts, 531 SSE timeouts, 541 connects, 52 HTTP403. PRIMARY afternoon Oct15 sample had 1624 lease writes and RTDB heartbeat 212 HTTP401+1408 HTTP403. Local attempts are not billable totals.

RTDB screenshot ~37k rule denies prove some requests reach Firebase and fail security evaluation; HTTP403 alone cannot distinguish proxy vs rules, so attributing every refusal to Office firewall is invalid. Need sanitized path/error/claim diagnostics, no broadening rules. 1.63KB stored/1% load does not suggest capacity saturation; RTDB download 25.31MB includes overhead and is not established as exactly one-day usage.

Across bounded Android HTTP summaries, MAX per device/hour/route/error gives lower bound 2447 RESULT_ACK_NOT_FOUND (1454 Oct15 + 993 early Oct16) affecting 29 devices. Endpoint covers RECEIVED/DISPLAYED/ACKNOWLEDGED. Overlay ACK quarantine already exists; MainActivity drainNotificationReceipts keeps unscoped pendingResultEvents on every exception and lacks comparable single-flight. This is a strong source candidate for repeated stale receipt calls, not proof of root cause for all requests or frozen overlays; affects Worker/DO/PDA energy, not direct Firestore reads.

Recommended staged design: first remove proven unused read and futile RTDB error/reconnect amplification; then select ONE steady-state liveness transport for responsible PRIMARY/NEXT_A (and required warm standby) set. RTDB only when responsible peers support it, shared Firestore lease listener if any require Office Firestore-only. Keep Firestore roles/generation CAS and confirmation carrier, WMS readiness/fences, pending watchdog, ACK/idempotency, FCM and no-offline business. entries.topic: Whole Agent–PDA flow audit and network-adaptive Agent upgrade design requested by Owner
facts: Owner asks to analyze both directions of PDA-Agent communication, Picklist confirm, call specialist, chat, kick and Picker online, with an Agent upgrade that automatically selects efficient model behavior when PRIMARY changes network. Current instruction is analysis/design, not approval of an unseen implementation or deployment.

Fresh main7ec91a75 and PR60609073318 manifest/full-bootstrap, current source and CI rechecked. All28 working-head checks completed with no failures, including authority/continuity; technical checks do not prove device/network/billed usage. No new provider screenshots or log-window collection claimed; E015 evidence remains controlling usage sample.

Current Android RelayPocClient always creates a Firestore relay_poc_jobs PENDING document, retries same UUID after bounded server verification, listens exact document for one terminal ACK and performs one final server read when necessary. PRIMARY uses gRPC payload + REST watchdog, ingress and pre-WMS role/generation checks, browser semantic UI, shared Picklist guard and one durable terminal job commit. RTDB is HA liveness only, not the current ordinary-network Picklist business carrier.

Important timing constraint: ACK await loop is20s after create, with separate auth/create recovery budgets; mutation admission fence is request age<12s, pending cutoff~20s, HA suspect threshold15s. Therefore standby takeover after suspicion cannot guarantee every already-waiting request completes within its first attempt; PRIMARY network-mode transition should be faster than waiting for death. Solo physical disconnection/WMS-unready cannot guarantee uninterrupted realtime. No deadline or offline-transaction expansion authorized.

Calls/chat/kick may originate from any properly authorized ADMIN/PICKPACK_ADMIN Agent, not PRIMARY-only. Call uses exact target active-call conditional write/60s shared lock/originating Agent resolve, exact PDA listener plus same-ID FCM. Chat uses per-UID session-control write plus legacy picker_alerts FCM path,200chars/30min; PDA confirmation is local dismiss with no server read receipt. Group sends per target with UID/generation validation; batching does not make N document writes cost1.

New source-backed Office gap: KickPickerUser requires server Core revoke first, but D160Resilience.TryD160WorkerRevokeOnce only POSTs Worker directly; existing Apps Script doPost has no revoke action and this callsite does not use D168NetworkRoute. If Office blocks Worker, equivalent kick is not established. Firestore-only UI logout must not replace server revocation; cron5m reconciliation is recovery, not the realtime kick path.

Proposed Office server-command choices: minimal allowlisted action on existing Apps Script gateway has shared UrlFetch quota dependence; preferred longer-term rare-command Google event bridge can call authoritative Worker and return same-ID receipt without polling, but needs Owner-approved handler/trigger, resource reconciliation, actor binding/auth-context/rules, server RBAC and target-session verification. No resource was created, endpoint probed or role expanded. Never persist bearer/session tokens in Firestore command documents.

Picker-online source is ACTIVE Android session + matching enabled FCM registration; transient socket disconnect intentionally does not remove session. Multiple representations currently coexist: direct presence projection, single-slot presence job+PRIMARY ACK, Pickers inside agent_sync and periodic reconcile. D153 already hashes semantic fields and ignores last_seen; Picklist fallback already upserts once and tombstones protect logout. Do not add repeated presence writes per Picklist/ping or pretend these prior optimizations are new.

Recommend retaining Core session authority and one versioned Office-readable presence projection, then removing duplicated projection/control-job/UI writes only after all Agent capabilities and removal/retry recovery are proven. Add separate session-valid, server-observed-connected and last-activity indications without automatic logout on socket loss. Existing Android WebSocket ping20s can be reused; Core ticket types currently WEB/ANDROID and socket attachments lack session generation, so reliable per-session connectivity contract needs Service changes.

Recommended Adaptive Agent design decides by own network epoch, authenticated capability, role and operation, not PRIMARY SSID alone. Office/PDA SSID classification is local event-driven policy, not security/liveness authority. Choose RTDB or exact Firestore lease listener as a common transport for responsible HA peers; keep Firestore roles/CAS, jobs/ACK and per-Picker command lane. Use separate transport epoch for same PRIMARY network changes and retain leader generation unless authority changes. Bounded make-before-break/peer-ready handshake only, no permanent dual heartbeat.

Current Agent network event refreshes proxy; SSID UI timer is60s and Visible-gated, so autonomous tray-mode transport switching is not implemented merely because GetSsid exists. Proposed coordinator must run independently of UI, debounce events, cache capability per epoch, distinguish auth401/backend403/proxy403 and circuit failures; no synthetic periodic endpoint polling or automatic WLAN switch permission inferred from this request.

Deep optimization candidates include unused legacy query removal(E015), healthy-listener redundant GET suppression, semantic/no-op/duplicate presence fanout reduction, one-source chat-to-FCM publication using approved Functions change and same-ID background compatibility, plus scoped Android RECEIVED receipt404 repair. Preserve final ACK, WMS guard, FCM wake, kick server authority and result/logout contracts. Savings unmeasured; jobs934reads is only one collection, not total Picklist cost including empty watchdog/rules/coordination/guards.

Alternative full RTDB-business/Firestore-Office or Worker/DO job-hub+Office relay could redistribute operations but requires App+Agent+Service/rules/durable request registry/archive/version migration, common idempotency and new AGENT WS contract. Agent-only cannot make vc110 hardcoded Firestore send RTDB, and dual-write-everywhere may increase total cost. Not selected for first upgrade absent total-meter baseline and separate Owner approval to reopen critical carrier decision.

Design, flow/source map, normal/Office/mixed matrix, upgrade packagesA-D versus deferred carrier migrationE, requirement-component-contract-test-evidence matrix and rollback/field gaps are retained in docs/D169_AGENT_PDA_ADAPTIVE_MODEL_2026-10-16.md. No implementation, APK/EXE bump, WMS automation, Firebase/rules/resource mutation, PR merge or runtime deployment was undertaken.
alternatives: BASELINE_NO_CHANGE: measure with present carriers, retains known repeated reads and inconsistent cross-network HA.
RECOMMENDED_ADAPTIVE_CURRENT_CARRIERS: Agent waste/capability/lifecycle and coordinated HA; selectively upgrade server command bridge, chat fanout and presence/receipt with exact approvals.
OFFICE_COMMAND_GATEWAY_MINIMAL: add low-frequency explicit revoke action to existing registered Apps Script transport; bounded usage but shared quota remains.
OFFICE_COMMAND_GOOGLE_EVENT_BRIDGE: preferred quota-independent-from-Script direction for rare server-authoritative commands; handler/resource/IAM/rules and timing proof required before deployment.

facts: Owner provided paired ZIP from standalone SUPRA Network Tester v1.0 on Windows x64, labeled ordinary Internet (15:48:41-15:48:51) and corporate Office (15:49:10-15:50:13), 42 public endpoints x2 rounds each; original sensitive/raw probe details are not committed.

Ordinary network 84/84 DNS and raw TCP OK; 76 HTTP unauthenticated class, 4 auth-required class and 4 TLS-only MQTT-port class. Ably and Pusher WSS endpoint handshakes returned HTTP 101 on both rounds.

Corporate network 84/84 DNS OK, 10/84 direct TCP/HTTPS responses (5 Google-hosted APIs x2), other 74 raw TCP failed (54 timeout, 20 network errors). Firestore, RTDB, Worker Beta, FCM, PubSub, Apps Script, Ably, Pusher, Supabase and further providers failed raw TCP on both rounds. HTTP 404/401/400 on five Google endpoints is not authenticated permission or realtime evidence.

Prior Agent field observations and direct tester mismatch are not proof of new Firestore outage. Failure is evidence against direct Office transport, not any valid corporate-proxy route.

No candidate was proven operational over both networks, no tenant-specific authenticated duplex message, pubsub ack, retention, role/generation enforcement, FCM background wake, HA takeover, billing, network proxy tunnel or session-revoke behavior was tested. Costs cannot be guaranteed zero.

entries.topic: Owner proposes automatic RTDB usage when PRIMARY on ordinary Wi-Fi and Firestore mode when PRIMARY on Office Wi-Fi
facts: Owner requests RTDB no-cost usage limits and prefers automatic mode: PRIMARY ordinary Internet Wi-Fi uses RTDB/realtime listeners where eligible, PRIMARY Office Wi-Fi switches to Firestore reads/writes. No explicit new code or release authorization was issued; this is a proposed design direction under D169.

Official Firebase pricing 2026-10-16: RTDB Spark free 1 GB stored, 10 GB downloaded/month and 100 simultaneous connections; Blaze 1 GB stored free, up to 360 MB downloaded/day no cost (roughly 10 GB/month), then $1/GB download and $5/GB-month storage, max 200k simultaneous connections/database. RTDB has no per-document read/write line item, but billed bytes include handshake/SSL/protocol, read/write traffic, denied rules requests. See firebase.google.com/pricing and firebase.google.com/docs/database/usage/billing.

Firestore Standard listener changes are charged document reads, and document writes are separately metered; RTDB listener downloaded bytes and reconnection overhead are metered, so shifting suitable heartbeat/control signals can reduce Firestore operations without assuming zero billing.

Current Windows RtdbHaLiveness.cs documents RTDB for ephemeral liveness ONLY; FirestoreAgentLeaderCoordinator.cs retains generation/role/CAS authority and 10s heartbeat; Android RelayPocClient and FirestoreConfirmationTransport remain Firestore job/PickList one-document terminal ACK. Changing PRIMARY SSID alone cannot redirect vc110 Android hardcoded Firestore jobs to RTDB.

Office corporate direct probe did not reach RTDB; earlier Agent logs show 401/403 security/auth or proxy uncertainty. Do not treat SSID as proof and do not classify current Office RTDB denial as guaranteed firewall; keep existing authenticated Firestore route and fixed critical ACK until field proof.

Most important cross-network nuance: HA transport must be common to all responsible PRIMARY/NEXT_A peers; if PRIMARY is Internet but standby is Office, Firestore liveness remains required for correct failover. If both capable of RTDB, RTDB liveness may replace steady Firestore lease polling as per existing D169 adaptive proposal. Changing PRIMARY Wi-Fi is neither a reliable security predicate nor sufficient to choose the entire fleet mode; role, peer capability, network epoch and handover handshake are needed.

Any Admin Agent on Office can still call/chat/kick independent of who is PRIMARY, so its communication needs cannot be eliminated based on PRIMARY network. Server session revoke remains Worker/Core-authoritative and current Office Worker direct route is unproven.

A full dual-carrier PickList/ACK switch would require Android + Agent + server transaction registry and compatible migration, preserving same request ID, one terminal durable receipt, CAS/generation/WMS guards, failover and background FCM; D168 explicitly retains critical Firestore route pending later approved change.

Existing screenshot RTDB downloads 25.31MB in user-selected billing period (not a daily total), stored 1.63KB and 37k rule denies, so download capacity is not proven saturated and repeated rejected requests must be diagnosed. No field-backed cost savings estimate is yet available.
alternatives: PRIMARY_SSID_ONLY: reject as insufficient for mixed Agent HA and side-channel operations; risks split-brain and missed Office standby.

RESPONSIBLE_PEER_COMMON_MODE: select RTDB HA when all responsible peers have proven endpoint auth and healthy latency, else Firestore exact-lease listener; network-change events and bounded mode handshake, still fixed Firestore job/ACK until separate approved migration.

FULL_CARRIER_ADAPTATION: conditional RTDB PickList/notifications for Internet and Firestore for Office requires Android+Worker/Core+Agent unified registry and idempotency; do not activate from an Agent-only update.
open_questions: Does Owner want to optimize HA-only first (recommended), or pursue full PickList/ACK + contact channel carrier migration (higher risk/requires phased Android update)?
How should mixed normal-Office HA peers be grouped given current installed Agent versions/capabilities?
What is authenticated RTDB and exact Firestore listener stability via native Windows proxy on Office, by network transition, based on field traces?
Measure actual per-16h RTDB downloads (including denied/overhead) versus Firestore read/write over the same fleet and traffic profile.
